## Teaching Approach {.section-heading}

Teaching at Maastricht University is grounded in Problem-Based Learning (PBL) and
active engagement with real research problems. Courses are designed to help
students build not just content knowledge but the critical thinking and
methodological skills needed for independent scientific work, whether in
the lab, the clinic, or beyond.

Franc holds a University Teaching Qualification (UTQ), is PBL-certified, and successfully completed the FPN mentor training, and
the Maastricht University's Inspiring Educational Leadership Trajectory
(IEL). His courses and lectures have received high student satisfaction ratings
over the past years.

## Bachelor's Courses {.section-heading}

<div class="course-card">
<div class="course-head">
<p class="course-title">Lifespan Psychology</p>
<span class="role-badge">Course Coordinator</span>
</div>
<div class="course-meta">
<span class="meta-pill"><i class="bi bi-mortarboard-fill"></i> BSc Psychology</span>
<span class="meta-pill"><i class="bi bi-calendar3"></i> Period 5 · Apr-Jun</span>
<span class="meta-pill"><i class="bi bi-bar-chart-fill"></i> Year 1</span>
<span class="meta-pill"><i class="bi bi-people-fill"></i> ~450 students / yr</span>
</div>
<p class="course-desc">The course provides an in-depth analysis of critical developmental processes including perceptual, cognitive, linguistic, emotional, social, and motor development. Key clinical conditions, including ADHD, schizophrenia, obsessive-compulsive disorder, depression, and dementia are examined as well including psychological interventions, pharmacological treatments, and other emerging therapeutic modalities. By integrating developmental and clinical perspectives, the course provides a well-rounded view of human psychological development, variation within it, and potential paths for intervention.</p>
</div>


## Master's Courses {.section-heading}

<div class="course-card">
<div class="course-head">
<p class="course-title">Development of Cognition and Language</p>
<span class="role-badge">Course Coordinator</span>
</div>
<div class="course-meta">
<span class="meta-pill"><i class="bi bi-mortarboard-fill"></i> MSc Psychology</span>
<span class="meta-pill"><i class="bi bi-calendar3"></i> Period 2 · Oct-Dec</span>
<span class="meta-pill"><i class="bi bi-bar-chart-fill"></i> Master's</span>
<span class="meta-pill"><i class="bi bi-people-fill"></i> 50-80 students / yr</span>
</div>
<p class="course-desc">This course explores the typical and atypical development (dyslexia, dyscalculia) of higher-order cognitive processes that underlie learning and academic achievement. Students examine how core cognitive systems, including working memory, episodic and semantic memory, language, numeracy and mathematical reasoning, executive functions, and general intelligence, develop and interact over time.</p>
</div>

## Thesis Supervision {.section-heading}

We regularly supervise Bachelor's and Master's thesis projects related to
the lab's research themes. Topics typically involve neurodevelopmental
conditions, sensory processing sensitivity, and computational approaches to
mental health, using EEG data and/or questionnaire-based data across healthy
or clinical populations. To date, Franc has supervised over 60 Master's thesis students and numerous
Bachelor's students at Maastricht University, and has served as (Co-)Promotor
for four PhD candidates.

## Educational Leadership & Service {.section-heading}

Alongside his teaching, Franc holds several coordinating and governance roles
within the Faculty of Psychology and Neuroscience: he coordinates the Master's
programme in Developmental Psychology and the Faculty's EEG laboratories, serves
on examination and advisory committees, and mentors staff and PhD candidates.

- **Coordinator**, Master Developmental Psychology, FPN (2026-present)
